notes: Cliopatria has no Rozvi. Budget: one article (the state's), one thin page for Danamombe (no coordinates, 17th-18th century dating only). The page's own span is c. 1683-1866 (infobox: 'Surrender of Tohwechipi: 1866'); the dossier ends in 1838, when the page says the state was 'conquered and subdued ... by Mzilikazi's Ndebele', because later the Rozvi hold only a remnant (the upper Save Valley by 1857) that the page does not outline. The Rozvi remnant (Tohwechipi, to 1866) is the only Rozvi presence after 1838. Successor states named in the infobox but not entered as land: the Venda Kingdom (Changamire dynasty migrated south in the late 17th century), the Nambya state (Sawanga migrated north to the Lower Gwai in the early 18th century), the Shangwe Confederacy. Counterpart names without dossiers: ngoni groups (Zwangendaba, Nyamazana, Nxaba), Mpanga's Sotho. The Mutapa vassalage (1712, from the Mutapa page; the Rozvi page has 1702 raids) is only 'influence and vassalage' per the page, not full control. The Danamombe point is approximate (see capital note). Region names: Zimbabwe Plateau is the gazetteer's country-of-Zimbabwe alias.
